title: Hampta Pass Trek
content:
The Hampta Pass Trek, at 14,000 feet in Himachal Pradesh, is a stunning adventure that includes one of the most spectacular mountain crossings in the Himalayas. The trek is well-known for its spectacular contrasts: the lush green Kullu Valley, with its woods, meadows, and blossoming flowers, contrasts sharply with the dry, desolate landscapes of Lahaul and Spiti, which are noted for their steep terrain and brilliant blue skies. 

Starting in the lovely town of Manali, this six-day journey spans around 26 km and passes through a variety of landscapes, including thick woods, wide meadows, and flowing waterfalls. As you approach the pass, you'll encounter several ledges that add to the thrill and excitement. You'll notice stunning surprises like the Himalayan Blue Poppy, Pink wild Geranium, and changing forests of apple orchards, deodar, and oak trees.

 

Why this Trek?

 

  1. Stunning View: The trek offers a mesmerizing contrast from the lush green Kullu Valley to the barren, rugged landscape of Lahaul and Spiti. 
  2. Breathtaking Chandratal Lake: Experience the enchanting beauty of the alpine Chandratal Lake, a crescent-shaped marvel nestled in the hills at around 14,000 feet, perfect for trekking, and photography.
  3. Adventurous Terrain: Navigate diverse terrains, from dense forests and expansive meadows to cascading waterfalls and rocky paths. 
  4. Cultural Immersion: Encounter the unique culture of the inhabitants of Sethan, migrants from Tibet and Spiti Valley. 
  5. Thrilling Journey: The drive from Manali to Jobra, with its 30 hairpin bends, sets the tone for an exhilarating adventure.

[{"icon":"fa fa-check","title":"Best Time to Visit","desc":"

The best time to visit Hampta Pass is from mid-June to October. Trekkers can experience some snow during the months of May-June or September-October, and August is the sunniest month until it starts raining. Snow is there in the early days of the season and then it melts down completely by August. Rain is expected during the monsoons in Kullu-Manali valley but the sun will remain bright as usual. The temperature is likely to remain between 12 and 20 °C during the day, while at night temperature at the highest would be between -2 to 6 °C. In the latter part of the trekking season (Sep – mid-Oct), a bit of snowfall can also be expected. The temperatures during the day will remain between 12-18 °C and in the evenings will start getting cold with temperature dropping down from 4 to -6°C.

"},{"icon":"fa fa-check","title":"How to Reach Basecamp","desc":"

By Train: Joginder Nagar is the nearest railway station (166 km from Manali). The other suited railheads are at  Pathankot and Chandigarh.

By Road: Manali is well connected by road with Delhi, Ambala, Chandigarh, Dehradun, Haridwar, Shimla, and Chamba/Dalhousie. Regular buses and taxis are available between these stations.

By Air: The Kullu Manali airport at Bhuntar Town (about 50 km from Manali and 10 km from Kullu town) is the nearest airport for Hampta Pass. Indian Airlines and some private airlines have regular set-off flights to the airport. Chandigarh is the nearest International airport

Pack smart, trek safe!

Ensure you're prepared for every adventure with this essential checklist of gear and supplies. Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned trekker, the right equipment makes all the difference. Download checklist's pdf here

 

Basic Gear

Backpack with Rain Cover (40 - 50 ltr) Comfortable Shoulder Straps
Day pack with Rain Cover 20 - 30 ltr (If off-load opted)
Walking stick Advisable (At least one)
Water Bottle / Hydration pack 2 Bottles(1 liter each), Hydration Pack 1 (Pack) + Bottle
Small size tiffin/lunch box 1 Nos
Snacks Energy bars, dry fruits, electral/ors
Personal Medical Kit Consult your doctor

 

Clothing

T-Shirt (Synthetic quick dry) 1 Full & 1 Half sleeves
Fleece T-shirt 1 Nos
Wind stopper / Fleece jacket 1 Nos
Windproof Jacket 1 Nos
Down feather / Hollow jacket 1 Nos
Thermal inner (Upper and Lower) 1 Nos
Trek Pant (Synthetic quick dry) 1 Nos
Wind stopper / Fleece Pant Not required
Waterproof gloves Not required
Fleece / woollen gloves 1 Pair
Poncho / waterproof Jacket and pant 1 Nos

 

Head Gears

Head torch 1 Nos. (Avoid Hand torch)
Sun cap 1 Nos. (One that covers the neck as well)
Woolen cap 1 Nos.
Balaclava Not required
Buff / Neck-gaiters 1 Nos
Sunglasses UV with dark side cover, People who wear spectacles - (A)- Use contact lenses | (B)- Photo chromatic glasses

 

Foot Gears

Trekking shoes 1 Pair (Waterproof, high ankle with good grip)
Floaters / flip-flops 1 Pair
Cotton socks 6 pairs
Woollen socks 1 pairs
Gaiters 1 Pair (provides when required)
Micro spikes 1 Pair (provides when required)

 

Personal Utilities

Sunscreen cream 1 Nos
Moisturiser 1 Nos
Chap-stick / Lip balm 1 Nos
Toothbrush and toothpaste 1 Nos
Toilet paper & Wipes 1 Nos
Soap / hand sanitizers 1 Nos
Antibacterial powder 1 Nos
Quick dry towel 1 Nos

"},{"icon":"fa fa-check","title":"Quick Facts about Hampta Pass Trek","desc":"

Mobile Network:

  • The last point for mobile network connectivity is Prini.
  • After Prini, there will be no network throughout the trek.
  • The network will be available again only near Rohtang Pass and Manali on your return.
  • Inform your family and friends before leaving Manali, as you will be unreachable until Day 6.

Last ATM:

  • The last ATM is located at Prini, en route to the base camp.
  • No ATMs will be available after crossing the pass until you return to Manali.
  • Ensure you withdraw sufficient cash before heading to the trek.

Electricity:

  • There is no electricity available throughout the trek.
  • The only place to charge electronic devices is in Manali, before and after the trek.
  • Fully charge all devices before leaving and minimize usage.
  • Cold temperatures drain batteries quickly; carry extra batteries or power banks to avoid issues.
